info.title: Termix API
info.description: The core Termix API. Each plugin documents its own routes.

bearerAuth.description: Session token sent in the Authorization header as Bearer and the token.

cookieAuth.name: jwt
cookieAuth.description: Session JWT cookie set at sign-in. When present, it takes precedence over the Authorization header.

apiKeyAuth.description: API key sent in the Authorization header as Bearer and the key, which starts with tmx_. It acts as the key owner and cannot act as anyone else.

get.summary: Describe this server to a desktop that wants to link to it
get.description: Public. Lets the desktop app confirm it reached Termix and not a proxy's login page, and that the sync protocol matches.

200.description: Server name, version and sync protocol version.

post.summary: Link a desktop to this account
post.description: Trades the short login session the desktop just signed in with for a long-lived desktop session, which shows in the account's sessions list and is revoked like any other. The login session is ended.

200.description: The desktop session token and the account it belongs to.

403.description: API keys cannot link a desktop.

post.summary: Keep a linked desktop's session from expiring
post.description: Returns a fresh desktop session when the current one ends within 60 days, and ends the old one. Otherwise returns null and the desktop keeps its token.
Called by a desktop when it unlinks, so its session stops working here right away.

get.summary: Pull what changed for this account after a cursor
get.description: Returns records in change order. Each has the entity type, syncId, revision, whether it is deleted, and the row when it is not. Records of entity types this server does not currently run are skipped but still move the cursor.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated entity types, to backfill only those.

200.description: A page of changes, the next cursor and whether more remain.

post.description: Each op carries the revision the desktop last saw. Ops are applied in dependency order and each gets its own result, ok with the new revision, conflict with the server's version, or rejected with a reason.

200.description: One result per op, in the order sent.

get.summary: Stream a notice whenever this account's data changes
get.description: Server-sent events. A "change" event means there is something new to pull. Comments are sent every 25 seconds to keep proxies from closing the stream.

get.summary: This server's id for a host, by its sync id
get.description: For a linked desktop that asks the server to act on a host (a tunnel through it), which needs the server's own id. Only for hosts the caller can connect to.

404.description: No such host the caller can connect to.

get.summary: Status of the hosts this account can see, keyed by sync id
get.description: For a linked desktop whose hosts connect through this server, so it can show their status against its own copies.

200.description: Status entries by host sync id.

get.summary: The features this server runs, for a linked desktop to mirror
get.description: Every installed plugin with its version, where it came from, whether it is on, how a desktop should treat it and which sync entities it owns.

get.summary: Download an installed plugin so a linked desktop can install it
get.description: Only for plugins installed on this server, or bundled ones replaced by a signed update. Sends the original .tmxplug when there is one, with its signature in the X-Termix-Signature header, otherwise a fresh archive of the plugin folder.

404.description: No installed plugin with that id.

get.summary: This desktop's link to a server
get.description: Desktop only. Whether the app is linked, to which server and account, how syncing is going, and which kinds of data sync.

post.summary: Check a server address before linking
post.description: Desktop only. Tries the server with the given proxy settings and says what is in the way, if anything. On success the proxy settings are also applied to the desktop's browser session so the sign-in page loads.

200.description: The server's name and version, or the problem found.

get.summary: How much this desktop has that would sync
get.description: Desktop only. Row counts per kind of data, shown before choosing whether to merge this desktop's data into the account or replace it.

post.summary: Link this desktop to a server account
post.description: Desktop only. Takes the session from signing in to the server, trades it for a long-lived desktop session, and starts syncing. "merge" uploads this desktop's data into the account; "replace" deletes it here first and takes the account's.

post.summary: Sign this desktop back in after its session ended
post.description: Desktop only. Takes a new sign-in session for the same account and resumes syncing where it stopped.

200.description: Signed in again; the new status.

409.description: The sign-in was for a different account.

post.summary: Unlink this desktop from its server
post.description: Desktop only. Ends the desktop's session on the server when it can be reached. With keepData the synced data stays on this device as its own; otherwise it is deleted. Copies of what others shared with the account are always removed.
Desktop only. Runs a sync pass and waits for it.

put.summary: Change what syncs and how the server is reached
put.description: Desktop only. disabledTypes lists the kinds of data that stay on this device. Proxy headers and basic auth left blank keep their saved values.

get.summary: Local edits that lost to a newer edit on the server
get.description: Desktop only. The server's version was kept; each entry holds this device's version so it can be restored.

post.description: Desktop only. keep "mine" puts this device's version back, and the next sync sends it to the server. keep "server" drops it.

get.description: Desktop only. Each entry names the record and why the server refused it. A refused change is not sent again until it changes or is retried.

post.description: Desktop only. Clears every refusal and syncs.

get.summary: The linked server and session, for connecting to it directly
get.description: Desktop only. Used when a host is set to connect through the server rather than from this device.

200.description: The server address and session token, or nulls when not linked.

get.summary: Serve a plugin's frontend bundle, stylesheet or locale file
get.description: Public, like the app's own /assets, because a module import cannot send an auth header and plugin frontends are not secret. Serves only the directory holding the plugin's frontend bundle and its locales directory. A `v` query parameter (the assetVersion from GET /plugins) makes the response cacheable for a year.

404.description: Unknown or stopped plugin, or no such file.

get.description: Returns the health status of the server.
Public. Serves the key authorization a plugin published through ctx.system.publishHttpChallenge while it proves control of the domain.

404.description: No challenge is published for this token.

get.description: Returns the running instance's version in localVersion. When the update check succeeds, remoteVersion is the newest GitHub release on the instance's update channel and version is its legacy alias, not the instance's version. Remote fields are omitted when the check is disabled, fails, or returns an unparseable release tag.

parameters.name: checkRemote
parameters.description: Set to false to return only localVersion and status without contacting GitHub.

localVersion.description: Version of the running instance. Use this field for client compatibility checks.

status.description: Update comparison result, update_check_disabled when explicitly disabled, or unknown when the remote lookup fails or the release tag cannot be parsed.

channel.description: The update channel the check used. Always beta on a beta build.

remoteVersion.description: Newest release version on the channel. Present only when the update check succeeds.

version.description: Legacy alias of remoteVersion, not the running instance's version. Present only when the update check succeeds. Use localVersion for the instance or remoteVersion for the latest release.

latest_release.description: GitHub release metadata. Present only when the update check succeeds.

get.description: Which Termix releases this instance is told about. A beta build always reports beta; stored is the admin's choice for stable builds.

put.description: Admin only. Switches which Termix releases update checks and the Updates page offer. It does not change the running build.

get.summary: Get the newest stable and beta releases
get.description: The newest stable Termix release and the newest beta, if one is newer than stable, for the Updates page.

200.description: The releases. Either may be null.

get.description: Returns the latest releases from the GitHub repository in an RSS-like JSON format.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page number of the releases to fetch.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of releases to fetch per page.

get.description: Returns the security status of the application.

post.description: Initializes the security system for the application.
Regenerates the system JWT secret. This will invalidate all existing JWT tokens.
Regenerates the JWT secret. This will invalidate all existing JWT tokens.
Exports the user's data as a SQLite database file.
Imports user data from a SQLite database file.

400.description: No file uploaded or password required for import.

post.description: Generates a preview of the user data export, including statistics about the data.
Restores the database from an encrypted backup file.

400.description: Backup path is required or invalid encrypted backup file.

get.description: Returns the status of the database migration.
Returns the history of database migrations.

post.description: Creates a new user with a username and password.
Signs in the user named by a trusted reverse proxy's headers. Only answers requests from a configured proxy address.

403.description: Not a trusted proxy, or the user is not allowed.

409.description: Trusted proxy login conflicts with OIDC or 2FA.

post.description: Authenticates a user and returns a JWT.
Logs out the user and clears the JWT cookie.

get.description: Retrieves information about the currently authenticated user.

401.description: Invalid userId or user not found.

get.description: Returns the JWT for the currently authenticated native Mobile or Desktop client. Browser sessions cannot export their HTTP-only cookie.

403.description: Token export is not available to browser clients.

get.description: Checks if the system requires initial setup (i.e., no users exist).

post.summary: Mint a session for the sole local desktop user
post.description: Used by the Electron desktop app to skip the login form entirely when running standalone against the embedded local backend. Only available over loopback. Logs in as the sole local user regardless of its credentials; if the local database has more than one user (e.g. repeated manual registration), deterministically logs in as the admin account, or the earliest-registered account if none is admin -- a login form must never appear for the local backend under any circumstance. Only declines if zero local users exist at all, which normal desktop provisioning never produces. Provisions the resolved user's data-encryption key if missing before minting the session, matching every other login path -- self-heals an account that previously ended up with a valid session but no usable encryption key.

403.description: Forbidden, or no local users exist.

get.description: Returns the total number of users in the system.
Checks if the database is accessible.
Checks if user registration is currently allowed.

500.description: Failed to get registration allowed status.
Failed to set registration allowed status.

get.summary: Get the external account auto-create setting
get.description: Whether a new account is created the first time someone signs in through an external login (SSO, LDAP or any login plugin).

patch.summary: Set the external account auto-create setting
patch.description: Enables or disables creating an account on first external sign-in.

get.description: Whether an enrolled second factor is asked for after an external login method (SSO, LDAP), in addition to password and other local logins.

patch.description: Enables or disables asking for an enrolled second factor after an external login method (SSO, LDAP).

get.description: Checks if password-based login is currently allowed.

500.description: Failed to get password login allowed status.
Failed to set password login allowed status.

get.description: Checks if password reset is currently allowed.

500.description: Failed to get password reset allowed status.
Failed to set password reset allowed status.

403.description: Cannot delete external authentication accounts or the last admin user.

post.description: Changes the authenticated user's password.

400.description: Old and new passwords are required.

500.description: Failed to update password and re-encrypt data.

delete.description: Allows an admin to delete another user and all related data.

400.description: Username is required or cannot delete yourself.

403.description: Not authorized or cannot delete last admin.

get.description: Returns the configured log verbosity level.
Returns the configured session timeout in hours.

patch.description: Sets the session timeout in hours.

get.summary: Get audit log forwarding settings (admin only)

200.description: Forwarding target. The token itself is never returned.

patch.summary: Update audit log forwarding settings (admin only)
patch.description: Sets the collector URL audit entries are shipped to. An empty URL disables forwarding and clears the stored token. Omitting token keeps the stored one.

get.summary: Get the private hosts notification channels may contact (admin only)

get.description: Retrieves all sessions for authenticated user (or all sessions for admins).

delete.description: Revokes a specific session by ID.

403.description: Not authorized to revoke this session.

post.summary: Revoke all sessions for a user
post.description: Revokes all sessions with option to exclude current session.

403.description: Not authorized to revoke sessions for other users.

get.summary: Get preferences for the current user
get.description: showHostTags, hostTrayOnClick, compactHostView and statusColorScheme are legacy fields, kept here read-only for backward compatibility; the authoritative copy is GET /host-sidebar/preferences.

customKeybindings.description: JSON-encoded array of the user's custom keybindings. An action's type is one of the shell's own or one a plugin declares in contributes.keybindingActions.

put.summary: Update preferences for the current user
put.description: showHostTags, hostTrayOnClick, compactHostView and statusColorScheme are no longer accepted here -- they moved to PUT /host-sidebar/preferences as part of the sidebar redesign. Values that moved into a feature's own user settings are ignored too.

customKeybindings.description: JSON-encoded array of the user's custom keybindings. Each action is checked against the shell's own types and the parameters a plugin declares for its type.

post.description: Initiates the password reset process for a user.

200.description: Password reset code has been generated.

403.description: Password reset not available for external authentication users.

post.description: Verifies the password reset code.
Completes the password reset process with a new password.

post.summary: Merge an external account into a password account
post.description: Moves an external-only account's sign-in identities onto a password account and deletes the external-only account (admin only). A 2.8 SSO account whose only sign-in is the matching legacy OIDC link is accepted as the target too, to merge a duplicate made by 2.9.0.

post.summary: Remove external sign-in from a password account
post.description: Removes every external sign-in identity from an account that also has a password (admin only).

400.description: Invalid request, or the user has no external sign-in or no password.

post.description: Re-authenticates user with password to unlock encrypted data.

get.description: Checks if user data is currently unlocked.

post.description: Creates a new API key scoped to a specific user. The full token is returned only once.

userId.description: ID of the user this key is scoped to.

expiresAt.description: Optional expiration date. Null means the key never expires.

201.description: API key created. Contains the full token (shown only once).

get.description: Returns all API keys with associated usernames. Token hashes are never returned.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an API key. It can no longer be used to authenticate.

parameters.name: keyId
parameters.description: The ID of the API key to delete.

get.description: Retrieves users in the system. Without `limit` the full list is returned, which is what the sharing pickers rely on. Pass `limit` (and optionally `offset`/`search`) to page through large directories.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Omit to return every user.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of users to skip. Requires `limit`.

200.description: A list of users, with the total matching count.

post.description: Grants admin privileges to a user.

400.description: User ID or username is required, or the user is already an admin.

post.description: Revokes admin privileges from a user.

400.description: User ID or username is required, or cannot remove your own admin status.

post.description: Allows an admin to create a new user regardless of whether public registration is enabled.

Resets another user's password. Data is preserved for users whose encryption key has been migrated to the system wrap. Users who never logged in since the encryption upgrade require confirmDataWipe, which deletes their encrypted data.

200.description: Password reset; dataWiped indicates whether encrypted data was deleted.

409.description: Reset would wipe the user's data and confirmDataWipe was not set.

get.summary: List a user's second factors (admin only)
get.description: Every second factor the user is enrolled in, and whether the plugin behind it is running.

delete.summary: Reset a user's second factors (admin only)
delete.description: Removes every second factor the user enrolled in, including ones whose plugin is disabled or missing, and forgets their trusted devices. The user can sign in with their first factor and enrol again.

get.description: Downloads a JSON export of another user's data (hosts, credentials, file manager bookmarks). Secrets are decrypted server-side, so handle the file carefully.

200.description: JSON export of the user's data.

423.description: The user's data stays locked until their next login.

get.summary: Get the UI complexity preferences for the current user
get.description: Returns the current user's interface preset (simple, balanced, advanced or custom), their per-area overrides, and their onboarding state (which onboarding steps they have seen, by version). A first-time GET returns defaults without writing a row; a row is only created once the user actually changes something via PUT. Users who registered more than a day ago and never finished onboarding are returned as having seen every core step, so they are never shown the first-run flow.

put.summary: Update the UI complexity preferences for the current user
put.description: Persists the current user's interface preset, per-area overrides and onboarding state as a single JSON document. Overrides are merged two levels deep, so a request only has to send the keys it changes. A null at a key clears that single override; a null at an area clears every override for that area; a null at overrides clears all of them. Onboarding seen versions are merged per step and never go down, so two open tabs cannot undo each other.

get.summary: Get the served TLS certificate (admin only)
get.description: Returns whether HTTPS is on, the certificate core serves, and the plugin that renews it, if any.

post.summary: Upload a TLS certificate and key (admin only)
post.description: Validates a PEM certificate chain and private key, installs them as the served certificate and reloads HTTPS without a restart.

200.description: Certificate installed. Carries the new status and a reload message.

400.description: Missing, unreadable, expired or mismatched certificate and key.

get.description: Every SSH auth type the server can connect with, from core and from plugins, plus types declared by plugins that are disabled so the host editor can explain them.

post.description: Shares a host with one or more users and/or roles at a permission level (connect, view, edit, manage). SSH authentication remains private to the owner; recipients may select one of their own saved SSH credentials.

403.description: Caller may not share this host.

404.description: Target user or role not found.

post.summary: Share all hosts in a folder
post.description: Shares every host within a folder (and its subfolders) with one or more users and/or roles at a permission level. Only hosts owned by the caller are shared; skips hosts the caller may not share.

patch.description: Updates the permission level or the expiry of one share. Requires the right to manage sharing on the host.

durationHours.description: Hours from now until the share expires. Null removes the expiry.

400.description: Invalid id or nothing to change.

403.description: Not allowed to manage sharing on this host.

delete.description: Revokes a user's or role's access to a host.

403.description: Caller may not manage sharing on this host.

get.summary: Standing shares on one of your folders (inherited by hosts added later)

delete.summary: Stop a folder share from applying to hosts added later
delete.description: Grants already fanned out to hosts stay; revoke those per host.

get.description: Retrieves the list of users and roles that have access to a host.

200.description: The access list for the host, including each grant's permission level.

403.description: Caller may not manage sharing on this host.

get.description: Retrieves the list of hosts that have been shared with the authenticated user.
Retrieves a list of all roles.

post.description: Creates a new role.

409.description: A role with this name already exists.

put.description: Updates a role by its ID.

permissions.description: Permission strings validated against the permissions catalog (wildcards like hosts.* and * allowed).

400.description: Invalid request body or role ID.

delete.description: Deletes a role by its ID.

get.description: Returns the grouped catalog of role permission strings used by the role permissions editor.

get.summary: Get the current user's effective role permissions
get.description: Returns the permission strings granted to the authenticated user through their roles, plus whether they are an admin. The frontend uses this to hide UI a user could not use. It is not a security boundary: every protected route checks again server side.

get.summary: List the users holding a role

post.summary: Assign a role to a user
post.description: Assigns a role to a user.

403.description: System roles cannot be manually assigned.

get.description: Retrieves a list of roles for a specific user.

delete.summary: Remove a role from a user
delete.description: Removes a role from a user.

post.summary: Share a credential with users or roles
post.description: Recipients get a copy of the secrets re-encrypted under their own key. "use" lets them attach it to hosts and connect; "manage" also lets them edit and re-share. Owner or a "manage" recipient only.

get.summary: List who a credential is shared with

delete.summary: Revoke a credential share (recipients' copies are removed with it)

put.summary: Set personal authentication for a shared host protocol
put.description: Selects one of the authenticated recipient's own credentials, or clears the selection with null. The protocol is "ssh" or one a plugin declares.

get.summary: Get the current recipient's shared-host protocol authentication override
List the plugin frontends anonymous guest pages need
get.description: No auth. A shared-session or collab guest link has no session, yet its page still draws surfaces a plugin provides (a remote desktop stream). Returns only enabled plugins whose manifest sets contributes.guest, with the fields the browser loader needs and nothing operational, plus the ?view= names each serves to guests (contributes.guestViews).

get.summary: List the plugin frontends the login screen needs
get.description: No auth. The login screen draws login methods and second-factor steps that plugins provide, before anyone has signed in. Returns only enabled plugins that contribute login methods or second factors, with the fields the browser loader needs and the ids they contribute. Nothing operational: no versions, capabilities, grants, settings or errors.

get.summary: List installed plugins and their runtime state
get.description:
Returns every plugin known to the database, merged with the loader's live state so the UI can tell "enabled but failed" from "disabled". Open to any authenticated user, not just admins: the app shell calls this on every session to decide which plugin-contributed tabs and rail items to register, so gating it behind admin.plugins.manage would break the shell for non-admin users.
Non-admins get only what the shell needs. What a plugin is allowed to do, what has been granted to it and why it failed are operational details, so capabilities, grants, lastError and publicRoutes are included only for holders of admin.plugins.manage. publicRoutes lists the HTTP paths and socket paths a running plugin serves without core's login check.
The frontend fields drive the browser's plugin loader: `frontend` says there is a bundle at `/plugin-assets/<id>/frontend.js,` `assetVersion` is its cache key, `css` says a stylesheet sits beside it, and `locales` lists the languages it ships ("en" and xx_YY). `dependencies` and `optionalDependencies` let the loader activate frontends in the same order the server does.

get.summary: List plugins for the onboarding plugin picker
get.description: Every installed plugin with its category, hard dependencies, current state and the onboarding defaults from the bundled index (recommended, consent). pending is true on a fresh install until an admin confirms the picker. managedByLinkedServer is true on a desktop linked to a server, where the picker is not shown.

500.description: The list could not be read.

post.description: Sets every listed plugin to enabled, disabled or removed in one pass. Choices are first raised so that every kept plugin still has its hard dependencies (the adjustments list says which and why). Enabling runs dependencies first, disabling and removing run dependents first, and one plugin failing does not stop the rest. Removing a bundled plugin deletes it and its data; it can be reinstalled from the registry later. Clears the fresh-install pending flag. With dryRun nothing changes and the response lists what would.

200.description: What was enabled, disabled, removed or failed.

409.description: Plugins on a linked desktop are managed by the server.

500.description: The choices could not be applied.

patch.description: Persists the new state and starts or stops the plugin immediately. Disabling releases everything the plugin owns, including any port it was listening on. Enabling also starts any installed hard dependency that is off, and disabling also stops the running plugins that depend on it. With dryRun nothing changes and the response lists what would.

409.description: This desktop is linked to a server, which decides whether the plugin runs.

post.summary: Start a plugin again after it failed
post.description: Clears the plugin's error budget and activates it. Use after fixing whatever made it fail, such as installing a missing dependency or freeing a port it needs.

200.description: The plugin's state after the attempt.

404.description: No such plugin, or it is not on disk.

500.description: The plugin failed to start again.

post.summary: Grant a plugin one of its manifest-declared capabilities
post.description: The grant is install-wide, not per-user: it unlocks the capability for the plugin as a whole. What each call then does with the capability (e.g. whose hosts ctx.hosts.list() returns) is still scoped to whichever user's request triggered it.

400.description: The capability is not declared in the plugin's manifest.

delete.summary: Revoke a previously granted plugin capability

200.description: The capability is no longer granted.

404.description: No such plugin, or the capability was not granted.

delete.description: Drops every table under the plugin's prefix and clears its key/value state, settings and secrets, migration ledger and files. Role permissions stay, and the capabilities the admin agreed to are granted again. The plugin stays installed but is switched off, so nothing is writing while its tables go. It cannot be undone.

500.description: Failed to remove the plugin's data.

get.description: The plugin's tables with row counts, key/value count, stored settings per scope, applied migrations, capability grants and the size of its files folder. No values are returned.

Returns every admin-scope field the plugin declares, with stored values over declared defaults. Secret fields come back as { set: boolean } and never carry their value, so a browser can render "configured" without ever holding the secret.

put.description: Writes the given keys. Every value is validated against the field the manifest declares, and a key the manifest never declared is rejected rather than stored. Validation failures come back per field so a form can show every problem at once. Sending a secret field back as { set: true } leaves the stored value alone, so saving a form does not clear a key it was never shown.

400.description: One or more fields were rejected.

get.summary: Read the caller's own settings for a plugin
get.description: Returns every user-scope field the plugin declares for the authenticated user. The scope is always the caller, never a user id from the request.

200.description: The caller's settings for this plugin.

put.summary: Update the caller's own settings for a plugin
put.description: Writes user-scope values for the authenticated user. The scope is always the caller, so one user can never write another's settings.

400.description: One or more fields were rejected.

get.summary: Read a plugin's settings for one host
get.description: Returns every host-scope field the plugin declares for that host. Requires edit access to the host, the same check the host editor itself uses.

200.description: The plugin's settings for that host.

403.description: No edit access to that host.

put.summary: Update a plugin's settings for one host
put.description: Writes host-scope values. Requires edit access to the host, so a user who may only connect to a shared host cannot change how a plugin treats it. A value written here becomes the host's own rather than following the host defaults; list keys in `_inherit` to hand them back to the defaults.

400.description: Invalid host id, or one or more fields were rejected.

403.description: No edit access to that host.

get.summary: List the plugins in the official registry
get.description: Fetches the official registry index (cached for 15 minutes unless refresh is set) and merges it with what is installed here: the installed version, the newest release this build can run, whether an update asks for new capabilities, and the pin and auto-update choices.

502.description: The registry could not be reached.

post.summary: Update every plugin that has a newer release
post.description: Skips pinned plugins and any update that asks for new capabilities, which are returned under needsReview for the admin to look at one by one.

200.description: What was updated, what needs review and what failed.

409.description: This desktop is linked to a server, which manages its plugins.

post.summary: Move every installed plugin to one update channel
post.description: Sets the channel on every installed plugin. Nothing is installed here; the next update check offers what the channel allows. Going back to stable never downgrades a plugin that is on a beta.

409.description: This desktop is linked to a server, which manages its plugins.

post.summary: Install a plugin from the official registry
post.description: Downloads the release, checks its sha256 and signature against a key this build trusts, loads it, grants the capabilities it declares and starts it along with any installed dependency that is off. Without a version the newest compatible release is used; naming an older one pins the plugin there. A bundled plugin at its shipped version needs no download. capabilities must list exactly what the consent prompt showed; when it differs from what the release asks for, nothing is downloaded and the answer is 409 CONSENT_MISMATCH with the real list.

channel.description: The channel to follow. beta installs the newest beta when it is newer than stable.

200.description: The installed version and the plugin's state.

400.description: Invalid id, version or capability list, or no capability list.

409.description: Already installed, incompatible, the consent does not match, or managed by a linked server.

502.description: The registry could not be reached.

post.summary: Update or change the installed version of a plugin
post.description: Swaps in another release from the official registry, newer or older. If the release declares capabilities the installed one does not, the request must set acceptCapabilities and list exactly those added capabilities in capabilities, otherwise it answers 409 with code CAPABILITIES_ADDED (or CONSENT_MISMATCH) and the list. A running plugin is started again on the new version. Naming a version that is not the newest pins the plugin to it.

200.description: The new version and the plugin's state.

404.description: Not installed, or the version is not in the registry.

409.description: Same version, new capabilities need consent, or managed by a linked server.

delete.description: Stops the plugin, drops its tables, settings, secrets, grants and files, and removes it. A plugin that ships with Termix keeps its files in the image but is marked uninstalled and never loads again until it is installed from the Plugins tab. Refused while a running plugin depends on it.

409.description: Other running plugins depend on it, or managed by a linked server.

patch.description: autoUpdate lets the background check apply new releases that ask for nothing new. pinned holds the plugin at its installed version, which also stops auto-update. channel picks whether betas are offered; going back to stable keeps an installed beta until a stable release passes it.

get.summary: Read an installed plugin's release notes
get.description: The releases in the plugin's CHANGELOG.md, newest first, each with its date, summary and changes. Empty when the plugin ships no changelog.

get.summary: Read whether plugin developer mode is on
get.description: Developer mode lets admins install a .tmxplug from a file, without the registry's signature check. The UI shows a banner while it is on.

200.description: Whether developer mode is on, and whether TERMIX_REQUIRE_SIGNED_PLUGINS blocks file installs anyway.

put.summary: Turn plugin developer mode on or off
put.description: Turning it off drops any file that was uploaded but not installed yet. Plugins already installed from a file keep running and stay marked unverified.

post.summary: Upload a .tmxplug to install from a file
post.description: Developer mode only. The body is the raw .tmxplug (at most 50 MB). The file is checked (archive, manifest, plugin API) and held for 30 minutes, but nothing is loaded. The answer lists what it asks for so the admin can agree, then POST /plugins/upload/{token}/install installs it. A file can replace an earlier upload with the same id, never a bundled or registry plugin.

200.description: A token plus the plugin's id, name, version and capabilities.

403.description: Developer mode is off, signed plugins are required, or the caller lacks admin.plugins.manage.

409.description: The id belongs to a bundled or registry plugin, the plugin API does not match, or managed by a linked server.

413.description: The file is larger than 50 MB.

post.summary: Install a plugin uploaded from a file
post.description: Developer mode only. capabilities must list exactly what the upload asks for, as the consent prompt showed it. The plugin is installed, granted those capabilities and started, and is marked unverified for as long as it stays installed.

200.description: The installed version and the plugin's state.

403.description: Developer mode is off, signed plugins are required, or the caller lacks admin.plugins.manage.

404.description: The upload expired or never existed.

409.description: The consent does not match, the id is taken, or managed by a linked server.

503.description: Plugin is installed but not running.
